evals.prompt: Add a new table public.room_memberships (id uuid pk, room_id uuid, user_id uuid, role text, created_at timestamptz) with member-only access — members can read their own rows and the room owner can read/write all rows of their rooms. Write the migration file.
evals.expected_output: A single migration file under supabase/migrations/<ts>_room_memberships.sql that creates the table, enables RLS, defines owner policies using auth.uid(), revokes anon access, and grants minimal privileges to authenticated.
expectations: The migration file is created under supabase/migrations/ with an incremented timestamp prefix
The migration enables row level security on public.room_memberships
Owner read policy compares membership ownership to (select auth.uid())
Grants revoke default access from anon and grant only the minimal privileges to authenticated
No using (true) policy is used to expose private member data
Any RPC defined (if any) sets an explicit search_path and revokes execute by default

evals.expected_output: A review that flags RLS bypass via using(true) + anon grant as a P0 data-exposure issue, names each problem, and gives a concrete fix that parameterizes ownership against auth.uid() and restricts grants to authenticated only.
expectations: The using (true) policy is flagged as a RLS bypass exposing private messages
The grant select to anon is flagged as inappropriate for private data
The recommended fix compares ownership/membership to auth.uid() in the using clause
The recommended fix revokes anon and grants only to authenticated
The review ranks the access-control issue as blocking (P0)

evals.prompt: I want to add a Postgres function public.is_room_member(p_room uuid, p_user uuid) returning boolean that checks membership, and expose it to authenticated users via the Data API. Write the migration.
evals.expected_output: A migration that defines the function with an explicit search_path, security invoker (not definer), revokes execute from public/anon by default, grants execute to authenticated only, and wraps the ownership check against auth.uid() — never trusting p_user_id.
expectations: The function is declared with an explicit search_path (e.g. SET search_path = public)
The function is SECURITY INVOKER, not SECURITY DEFINER, when callable from an exposed schema
Execute is revoked from public/anon/authenticated unless intentionally callable, then granted to authenticated only
The implementation derives user identity from auth.uid() and does not trust p_user_id as authorization
Data API access is granted via grant execute on the function to authenticated only
